name: Tetra: Serving Leech-Lattice Quantized LLMs at 2.7 Bits per Parameter
problem: Leech-lattice quantization gives good quality at 2 bits/weight, but the codebooks have more than 10^14 points - far too many for a lookup table, so earlier kernels read 4.8 bits/weight from memory to store 2 bits of code.
mechanism: A NEW codebook on the same Leech lattice, designed for lookup-table decoding: a 24-weight block still takes 48 bits, most of which index a 64-state TRELLIS of the Golay code plus one shared 16 KiB table. The kernel decodes a block with SIX TABLE LOADS AND TWO SMALL LOOKUPS inside the matvec and reads 2.148 bits per weight. For full models, retrain one scale per matrix row, store the matrices that lose the most as 4-bit integers, and pay for them with 4-bit embedding tables.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract, ALL numbers on ONE NVIDIA L40S): Qwen3-4B/8B/14B whole-model figures of 2.73 / 2.70 / 2.73 bits per parameter; MMLU (full test set) 63.37 / 69.58 / 75.66, i.e. 4.76 / 4.21 / 2.46 points BELOW 4-bit AWQ which runs at 5.3-6.0 bits/parameter; generate 113.8 / 95.0 / 57.2 tok/s in the authors' own engine; on GSM8K through the served kernel they lose 9.63 / 4.62 / 3.26 points to FP16. COMPRESSION RATIO: ~2.7 bits/parameter whole-model (~5.9x vs FP16). QUALITY COST: 2.46-4.76 MMLU points below AWQ, and up to 9.63 GSM8K points below FP16 at 4B - this is an honest, unusually complete quality statement.
